"@USER It is a lot of pressure put on runners from their communities and in my case, from myself, after how polarizing and traumatizing my last GDQ run was. I wanted to redeem myself, and I did everything right in this situation to avoid illness. Tested a week before and after symptoms."
"@USER I was a runner, youre aware of that, yeah?"

"@USER I fully get the intent you have and sympathize. Truly, theres a danger with mass gatherings in general still, even when everyone is masked up and standing at safe distances.   GDQ was far less crowded than my classes and my work environment. That is not the main issue."

"@USER I have done everything in my power to avoid this virus for over two years and I barely socialized at this event. I didnt even live in the hotel during the time, I was in an apartment with three people and I spent most of my time there."

"@USER There are risks I have to take just to get my education. There are risks I take just to get my next meal. Telling me that my illness here is something as a lesson is the least helpful thing to do, it dehumanizes me and neglects the larger image: Ive been at risk for years."

"@USER Listen really carefully: Im a college student. I am a student employee at the library.  Every day I face risks from COVID from higher powers pushing me to return in person and work in person and promote normal behavior when theres nothing normal about what Ive gone through."

"I cant explain how guilty this makes me feel. I truly did everything, tested as soon as I felt sick, isolated after even when I wasnt thinking I was positive for COVID, all that.  Yet the worst still happened. Fucking hell."

"So, despite the negative result in my rapid test a few days ago, I just went to a clinic and tested positive for COVID. I isolated after feeling sick at GDQ, but I suggest that anyone who met me best test themselves there.  I did all the precautions and measures possible"
